# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.
# iwe Enhancements — Implementation Plan

Source spec: `ENHANCEMENTS_SPEC.md`. Codebase reading was scoped to the files
the spec touches; line numbers below refer to current `main`.

The spec lists four work items; only the three iwe-internal ones are in
scope here. The task wrapper (item 4) is a separate shell tool and is not
covered by this Rust implementation plan.

---

## Part 1 — Implementation Plan

The order below matches the spec's "Implementation order" and respects the
internal dependencies (config struct → reader/writer → find filter → virtual
nodes).

### Phase 0 — Config plumbing (prerequisite for everything)

**File: `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`**

- `MarkdownOptions` (defined L19–27): add
  `#[serde(default)] pub bare_frontmatter: bool` field. Update
  `Default for MarkdownOptions` (L29–39) to set `bare_frontmatter: false`.
- `LibraryOptions` (L158–166): add
  `#[serde(default)] pub virtual_directories: bool`. Update
  `Default for LibraryOptions` (L174–185) to `virtual_directories: false`.
- `migrate()` (L559–): add a v3→v4 migration that just bumps the version and
  leaves both new fields absent (defaults apply). Bump
  `Configuration.version` ceiling, add `set_config_version(..., 4)` branch.
  This keeps existing `.iwe/config.toml` files round-tripping cleanly.
- `Configuration::template()` (L318–): no change needed (defaults are off);
  optionally add commented-out hints in the template TOML.

**Tests to add (`crates/liwe/tests/config_migration_test.rs`):**

- `migrates_v3_to_v4_adds_no_keys`: existing v3 config parses, version
  becomes 4, `bare_frontmatter` and `virtual_directories` both `false`.
- `parses_bare_frontmatter_true`.
- `parses_virtual_directories_true`.

**Dependencies:** none. Must land before Phases 1, 2, and 3 because they
read these fields.

---

### Phase 1 — Bare front matter support

#### 1a. Reader: pre-wrap bare headers with `---`

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`** (`MarkdownReader::document`, L26–33)

This is the cleanest injection point — it owns the `&str` content right
before it goes into `MarkdownEventsReader::read`. Add a helper:

```rust
fn wrap_bare_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> { ... }
```

Logic, gated on `markdown_options.bare_frontmatter`:

1. If `content` starts with `---` (optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM /
   leading whitespace? — see Open Question Q1) → return `Borrowed`.
2. Find first line. If it does not start with `title: ` (literal, including
   the space) → return `Borrowed`.
3. Find the index of the first blank line (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`, or EOF).
4. Split into `header_block` and `rest`. Return
   `Owned(format!("---\n{header_block}\n---\n\n{rest}"))`.

Then `MarkdownReader::document` calls `reader.read(&wrapped)` instead of
`reader.read(content)`. The downstream pipeline already handles
`MetadataBlock` events (see `reader.rs` L356, L386 — the
`Tag::MetadataBlock(_)` arms toggle `metadata_block`, and the `Text` arm
captures the YAML into `self.metadata`). No other reader changes required.

#### 1b. Writer: emit bare headers when configured

**File: `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs`**

`MarkdownWriter` already holds `options: MarkdownOptions` (L13). The
frontmatter is emitted at L41–49 in `block_events` for
`GraphBlock::Frontmatter(content)`, currently always as a
`MetadataBlock(YamlStyle)` event pair.

Two viable approaches:

- **Approach A (preferred):** When `self.options.bare_frontmatter`, do not
  push the `MetadataBlock` events at all. Instead, prepend the bare header
  text directly to the output string in `MarkdownWriter::write` (L21–30):
  call `cmark_with_options` for non-frontmatter blocks, then prefix
  `format!("{}\n\n", content.trim_end())` from the (single) Frontmatter
  block. Reason: pulldown_cmark_to_cmark always wraps `MetadataBlock` in
  `---`, so we cannot get bare output through it. Implementation: in
  `blocks_events`, partition out the leading `Frontmatter` block; in
  `write`, when bare mode and a leading frontmatter exists, write it raw
  first, then the rendered remainder.

- **Approach B:** Post-process the rendered string to strip the leading
  `---\n…\n---` and replace with bare lines. Brittle; reject.

Take Approach A.

#### 1c. Wiring callers

`MarkdownReader::document` already takes `markdown_options: &MarkdownOptions`
(`crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` L26), and `Graph::from_state` /
`Graph::from_markdown` (`graph.rs` L272, L347) thread it through. No
caller-site changes needed for the reader.

For the writer: instances are constructed in
`crates/liwe/src/model/tree.rs` and `crates/liwe/src/model/document.rs`
(grep for `MarkdownWriter::new`). They already receive `MarkdownOptions`
along the same path; just verify each site passes the loaded options rather
than `MarkdownOptions::default()`. (Spot-check needed during
implementation.)

- `reader_does_not_misparse_prose`: input `"This is a paragraph.\n\n# H\n"`

- `reader_still_handles_fenced`: input starting with `---` parses normally

- `writer_emits_bare_when_enabled`: round-trip

# iwe enhancements for structured note management

## Overview

Three changes to iwe (the Rust tool), plus a separate task-management wrapper. The iwe changes are general-purpose features useful to any knowledge graph; the wrapper adds project-specific workflow policy.

## Boundary principle

If someone using iwe for a photography knowledge base would find the feature useful, it goes in iwe. Metadata filtering, virtual directories — yes. Status transitions, gate enforcement — no. Those are opinions about workflow that belong in a wrapper.

---

## 1. Bare front matter support (iwe)

### Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: ` (literal, case-sensitive, space required after colon)
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line (strict `\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n` only — a line containing only whitespace is NOT a separator) are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives. No key whitelist needed — `title` as mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false`.

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (`crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` L26–33), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, call `wrap_bare_frontmatter(content)` which returns `Cow<str>`
- If content starts with `---`, return `Borrowed` (already fenced)
- If first line starts with `title: `, find first blank line, wrap the header block with `---` delimiters
- Otherwise return `Borrowed` (no front matter detected)
- Pass the wrapped content to `MarkdownEventsReader::read()`
- The downstream `MetadataBlock` handling already captures YAML into `Document.metadata` — no other reader changes needed

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled (`crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs`):
- In `block_events`, partition out the leading `GraphBlock::Frontmatter` block
- Do not push `MetadataBlock` events for it (pulldown_cmark_to_cmark always fences, can't bypass)
- In `write`, prepend the raw front matter text followed by a blank line before the rendered body
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand fenced front matter

### Config plumbing

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs`: add `#[serde(default)] pub bare_frontmatter: bool` to `MarkdownOptions`, default `false`
- Add v3→v4 config migration that bumps version (new fields use defaults)

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content

content.text: Updated (699 chars)

Fixed.

## Diagnosis

The bug was in bare-frontmatter detection, not in `--meta` matching.

`DocumentFinder::metadata_matches()` already handled YAML sequences correctly:

```yaml
depends:
  - foo
```

and fenced front matter worked because pulldown-cmark parsed it directly.

Bare front matter failed when the document began with:

```yaml
depends:
  - foo
```

because `wrap_bare_frontmatter()` only recognized bare front matter if the file started with literal `title: `. So a bare document whose first metadata key was `depends:` was parsed as normal Markdown body text, leaving no metadata for `iwe find --meta depends=foo` to match.

## Fix

Updated `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` so bare front matter is detected as a conservative YAML mapping block rather than requiring `title:` as the first key.

The new detector:

- still leaves already fenced `---` front matter unchanged
- takes the leading block up to the first true blank line
- verifies top-level lines look like metadata keys
- validates the candidate block parses as a YAML mapping with `serde_yaml`
- then wraps it with `---` so the existing metadata pipeline continues unchanged

## Tests added/updated

- Added regression coverage in `crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`:
  - bare frontmatter with:

    ```yaml
    title: Task A
    depends:
      - foo
    ```

    now matches `metadata_filters: depends=foo`.

- Updated `crates/liwe/tests/bare_frontmatter_test.rs`:
  - the old expectation that non-`title` first key is ignored is no longer correct
  - now verifies front matter is detected even when `title` is not the first key.

## Verification

- Reproduced the CLI failure before fix with a workspace containing:
  - fenced doc with `depends: [foo]`
  - bare doc starting with `depends:\n  - foo`
  - `iwe find --meta depends=foo -f keys` only returned fenced doc

- Verified after fix the CLI returns both:

```text
fenced
no-title
```

- Ran full test suite:

```text
cargo test
```

Passes. Full output exceeded tool display limit, but final suite/doc-test tail shows all passing.

## Current diff scope

Only focused files are modified:

```text
crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs
crates/liwe/tests/bare_frontmatter_test.rs
crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs
```

I also reverted unrelated `cargo fmt` churn from other files.
